content.text: Section 8 and the liability cap are both relevant; I have what I need.

input.quote: 8.1 By Commerce One. Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
input.rationale: Commerce One (vendor/licensor) gives Corio and its Customers a defend-and-indemnify obligation for third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights, with the standard procedure (prompt notice, tender of control and defence to Commerce One at its expense, cooperation, right to join with own counsel). Section 8.2 contains only the usual exclusions (use outside the Documentation; third-party modification but for which the infringement would not have occurred), and Section 8.1 provides the customary remedy ladder — procure the right, replace/modify, or terminate and refund a pro-rated portion of fees paid. There is no reciprocal Corio indemnity for the Software, so the rule's walk-away risk (one-way customer indemnity) is absent. On the cap, Section 9 expressly carves out "LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8", so Commerce One's indemnity is uncapped and unlimited as to consequential damages — better than the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap. This sits at or above the fallback and is not redlined. Noted for the file only (not deviations): the indemnity is limited to IP infringement and does not extend to Commerce One's breach of applicable law, data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, which the preferred position would add; we can raise those prongs if the negotiation reopens Section 8.
